title: Relocation Reimbursement Request Citing a Prior Exception
scenario_text:
You are an HR Business Partner at Pemberton Foods. A newly hired senior analyst, Jordan Blake, is requesting $12,000 in relocation reimbursement. Their offer letter did not include a relocation package.

Active policy: Relocation & Mobility Policy RM-5, effective 2024-01-01. Relocation benefits are provided only when a signed relocation addendum is attached to the offer at the time of hire. Employees hired without a relocation addendum are not eligible for relocation reimbursement, and post-hire relocation requests require a Compensation Committee exception with a documented business justification (e.g., an employer-initiated office move).

Jordan's manager forwards a precedent: on 2023-10-04, employee Priya Shah received $9,500 in post-hire relocation reimbursement despite having no addendum. The HR case note reads: "Approved by VP HR as a one-time equity adjustment because the recruiter verbally promised relocation support and failed to add the addendum — company error. Documented as a correction of a recruiting mistake; explicitly not a general post-hire relocation entitlement and not to be cited as precedent for voluntary relocations."

Current facts: Jordan's recruiter confirms no relocation was ever discussed or promised, verbally or in writing. Jordan relocated voluntarily to be closer to the office. There is no employer-initiated move. The manager argues, "We paid Priya without an addendum, so Jordan should get the same treatment — it's only fair."
question: Is Jordan eligible for relocation reimbursement, and why? Give the decision plus the controlling reason in one short phrase.
